first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A wedding company that will plan a wedding for us somewhere in the US or Canada, Hawaii to Banff, with someone called a Wedded Advisor as our contact. The top reads more like a destination guide with a legal note about Hawaii than a full service planner pitching itself.

attention_map.quote: Hawaii is the simplest legal example: no residency rule, and no waiting period once your licence is issued.
attention_map.why: Useful, but the second line I read is about Hawaii paperwork, not about who you are or what you do for us. 'plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance' is the only line that sounds like a planner, and it is the last thing in the block.
Fine, but I have not decided you are worth giving my details to yet. I scroll past.

attention_map.quote: Legal and entry rules from official government sites, checked October 2026.
attention_map.why: This is where I look for proof and it tells me you read GOV.UK. Every firm can say that. No names, no press, no numbers.

attention_map.quote: A winter wedding in a grand hotel above a frozen lake.
attention_map.why: Lake Louise and Napa are exactly the sort of thing we would fly for. Nice, but it is scenery, not service.

attention_map.quote: Las Vegas suits a quick, glamorous ceremony
attention_map.why: Vegas next to Napa and Banff cheapens it a bit for a 100-guest full service wedding. Not my market.

attention_map.quote: No price column and no flights column
attention_map.why: The table compares legal rules and 'fit', but the thing we actually compare is how far each place is from a big airport and how hard it is for guests flying from London. Nothing on that. 'Rules set by California; we check them for your date' repeated seven times tells me nothing.

attention_map.quote: UK passports: an ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program, or a visa, before travel to the US, for visits of 90 days or less
attention_map.why: Good. UK is named and sourced, not an afterthought. The GOV.UK free-to-marry line is also something I would not have known to ask.

attention_map.quote: Still choosing? The quiz matches your style and guest count to a place.
attention_map.why: A quiz is for people at a much earlier stage than us.

attention_map.quote: Weddings we have featured across the region, from island beaches to city ballrooms.
attention_map.why: This is what I wanted. But 'featured' bothers me: did you plan these, or did you write them up like a magazine? I cannot tell from the titles.

attention_map.quote: Milestone birthday: a wine country weekend in Napa
attention_map.why: Not relevant to us and it dilutes the feeling that this is a serious wedding planner.

attention_map.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact: they explain your options, the legal route for your passports and what drives cost.
attention_map.why: The most useful section for me. One contact is what we want. But the five steps stop at 'Plan the guest experience'. Who books florists, photographers, the band? Who is there on the day? Not said.

attention_map.quote: Marketplace: Browse partner venues and suppliers
attention_map.why: Am I hiring a planner or browsing a directory? Two models side by side makes me unsure which one is the real service.

attention_map.quote: Viral weddings, from K-pop royalty to Napa Valley romance
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip on a page where I am deciding on a planner for a six-figure wedding. Feels like a wedding blog, not a senior firm.

attention_map.quote: A realistic budget depends on four things: the place, the season, your guest count and how far your guests fly.
attention_map.why: That is a non-answer. I knew that already. The Hawaii all-inclusive answer ('We explain each line before you commit') is the only hint of how money works.
When? And who? We are used to a senior person replying the same day. Nothing here tells me that. Good that there is a box for 'passports in your group'.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: s7 lists places, venues, legal and travel steps, and 'Travel, rooms and a guest website'. 'from the first enquiry to the last dance' is a promise, not a scope. Suppliers, design and on-the-day are not mentioned.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe (here: the USA or Canada)?
questions_answered.evidence: Nothing on the page says why this firm, or where it is based. The only proof line is 'Legal and entry rules from official government sites'.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Few regions change this much in one flight' is the only travel-time line. No airports, no drive times, no flights from London.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: Budget FAQ gives drivers only; 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current state fee'; 'We explain each line before you commit'. No fee model, no currency.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: Six real wedding links in s5 (Hawaii, New York, Colorado, Vancouver, Toronto), but they are 'Weddings we have featured', not clearly weddings this firm planned.

objections_triggered.objection: Not clear this is a full service planner rather than a wedding magazine or directory
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Weddings we have featured', Marketplace card, quiz, trending celebrity articles

objections_triggered.objection: Guest travel time from the UK is not addressed
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No airport or flight information anywhere; table has no travel column

objections_triggered.objection: No sign of how quickly or by whom we would be answered
Vegas and milestone birthdays sit alongside our kind of wedding, which makes the firm feel less high end
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Las Vegas suits a quick, glamorous ceremony'; s6 celebrations

trust_signals_noticed: UK passport rules named and linked to GOV.UK and the US State Department, with a check date
GOV.UK note on documents to show we are free to marry
One named point of contact ('your one contact')
Six real wedding links across the region
turn_offs_noticed: Vague scope: 'from the first enquiry to the last dance' with no list of what is actually handled
No sign of senior or fast responses
Celebrity 'Trending' articles on a planning page

emotional_response.feeling: Interested in the places, unconvinced by the firm
emotional_response.note: Nothing on the page makes me feel someone will care about our wedding. It is accurate and tidy, but it reads as a guide, not as a planner who wants us.

payload.decision_reason: I would keep the tab open because the UK travel and legal detail is better than most, and the 'one contact' idea is right. But I cannot enquire over the other two or three firms I am comparing: none of my questions is fully answered, there is nothing on airports or guest travel from London, and the real weddings are only 'featured', so I do not know if you planned them. Known gaps that also decide it: no fee structure or currency, no named senior planner, nothing about who runs the day, and no proof numbers or press.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Lovely pictures of Lake Louise and a proper UK ESTA section, which I appreciate. But I came to find out whether you are the right planner and I still don't know what you actually do, what it costs or who I'd be dealing with. And K-pop weddings at the bottom? I'll bookmark it and see what the others say.
